headline: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5.5; Merz gets Fraktion backing after Landtag losses; Wunstorf drone may have carried explosives; Spangdahlem F-16 crashes with pilot ejecting.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5 — cheaper, faster, safer Opus
facts: Anthropic (Sep 22): Claude Opus 5.5 is the first Claude 5.5 release — performance framed near Claude Fable 5.1 while ~40% cheaper to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

Pricing: $4 / $20 per million input/output tokens (20% below Opus 5); cache reads $0.20/M (60% cut). Output claimed >30% faster; Pro/Max/Team five-hour limits raised, plus a bankable rate-limit reset.
Benchmarks (Anthropic table): Terminal-Bench 4.0 66.4%, FrontierCode v1.1 54.4%, CursorBench 4.0 57.8%, GDPval-AA 1846 Elo — ahead of Opus 5 and often GPT-6 Astra on coding/knowledge work.

Safeguards: biology/cyber/distillation filters similar to Fable 5.1 (sensitive work falls back transparently); external evals by METR and Frontier Design. Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 said to follow in coming weeks.
heise amplifies the DE read: efficiency + safety over pure benchmark theater; model id `claude-opus-5-5` live on Anthropic, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure.
stories.whyItMatters: First big frontier drop of the Claude 5.5 family — cost and safeguard pacing matter as much as the scores.

stories.title: Frei backs Merz in Fraktion after three Landtag setbacks
facts: Handelsblatt/dpa: Fraktionschef Thorsten Frei — “Der Bundeskanzler hat unsere Unterstützung” — after CDU losses in Sachsen-Anhalt, MV (out of Landtag) and Berlin (Linke took #1).
Merz accepted shared responsibility but stuck to reforms; speech called “geschäftsmäßig.” Ex-Fraktionschef Brinkhaus drew loud applause for criticizing Merz’s communication.
Frei wants the July SPD reform package done “in einem Rutsch”; pensions still sticky. Eight CDU Ministerpräsidenten already backed Merz Monday.
stories.whyItMatters: The Fraktion is closing ranks publicly even as internal communication blows keep landing.

stories.title: Wunstorf drone: investigators flag possible explosives near Bundeswehr base
facts: tagesschau (NDR/WDR/SZ, 17:00): a crashed drone found ~1 km from Fliegerhorst Wunstorf (~1 week ago) may have been explosives-laden — suspicious material a few meters from the wreck is still in forensics.
Generalbundesanwalt + BKA are on the case; construction resembles the Aug Leipzig/Halle attempt (custom build, at least one 3D-printed part). Wunstorf hosts the Luftwaffe’s A400M transport fleet.

Analysts think the wreck may have lain there a long time — possibly up to two years. The find was on today’s Nachrichtendienstliche Lage in the Kanzleramt. Berlin already blames Russia for Leipzig; Moscow denies.
stories.whyItMatters: If confirmed, it suggests another attempted strike on a critical German air-mobility hub — and a possible earlier miss.

stories.title: F-16 crashes at Spangdahlem; pilot ejects, jet destroyed
facts: SWR / USAFE: a 52nd Fighter Wing F-16 Fighting Falcon crashed ~14:30 on/near Airbase Spangdahlem (Eifel); the pilot ejected and is receiving medical care; cause under investigation.
DFS: crash after a four-ship training sortie — lead jet down returning to Spangdahlem; three diverted to Ramstein. Wreckage burned out; Bitburg-Prüm Katastrophenschutz assisted.
Witnesses in Speicher/Binsfeld/Beilingen reported a steep descent and a large smoke column. Spangdahlem also lost F-16s in training mishaps in 2019 (Zemmer) and 2006 (Oberkail).
stories.whyItMatters: A rare on-base fighter loss in the Eifel on a busy UNGA Tuesday — investigation still open.

stories.title: Apple’s persistent Settings “ads” for iCloud+/Music/AppleCare+ spark backlash
facts: TechRadar: iOS Settings shows sticky promos for iCloud+, Apple Music/TV trials, and AppleCare+ — often without a working dismiss, lasting weeks/months and leaving a badge on Settings.
HN (~356 pts): users compare it to Start-menu ads / enshittification; some iCloud+ subscribers still see the storage pitch, hinting at a bug or deliberate push.
Context: Apple’s services push after iPhone Duo / iPhone 18 Pro launches; further Visual Intelligence promos rumored. No official Apple response in the piece.
stories.whyItMatters: Premium OS framing collides with hard-to-dismiss first-party upsells.
